   394→def url_has_newer_version(url):
   395→    """Checks to see if a newer version of the resource at the URL is available
   396→    Always returns true if using Python2.7 due to lack of HEAD request support,
   397→    or if we have no caching information for the local version of the resource
   398→    """
   399→    metadata_filename = get_metadata_filename(url)
   400→
   401→    # Load in the cache
   402→    metadata = load_metadata(metadata_filename)
   403→
   404→    # Etag is a caching identifier used by S3 and Cloudfront
   405→    if "etag" in metadata:
   406→        cached_etag = metadata["etag"]
   407→    else:
   408→        # If we don't know the etag of the local version, we should force an update
   409→        return True
   410→
   411→    # Need to wrap this in a try, as URLLib2 in Python2 doesn't support HEAD requests
   412→    try:
   413→        # Make an initial HEAD request
   414→        req = Request(url, method="HEAD")
   415→        with urlopen(req) as res:
   416→            # If we have an ETag value stored and it matches the returned one,
   417→            # then we already have a copy of the most recent version of the
   418→            # resource, so don't bother fetching it again
   419→            if (
   420→                cached_etag
   421→                and res.info().get("ETag")
   422→                and cached_etag == res.info().get("ETag")
   423→            ):
   424→                LOGGER.debug(
   425→                    "We already have a cached version of url %s with ETag value of %s",
   426→                    url,
   427→                    cached_etag,
   428→                )
   429→                return False
   430→
   431→    except NameError:
   432→        # We should force an update
   433→        return True
   434→
   435→    # The ETag value of the remote resource does not
   436→    # match the local one, so a newer version is available
   437→    return True

   149→
   150→        Args:

   152→            resource_type (str): the :: version of the resource type

   154→            dict: returns the schema

   156→        if resource_type not in self._registry_schemas:

   160→            raise ResourceNotFoundError(resource_type, region)
   161→
   162→        reg = ToPy(region)
   163→        rt = ToPy(resource_type)
   164→
   165→        schema = self._schemas[reg.name].get(rt.name)
   166→        if schema is not None:

   169→        # dynamically import the modules as needed
   170→        self._provider_schema_modules[reg.name] = __import__(
   171→            f"{self._root.module}.{reg.py}", fromlist=[""]
   172→        )
   173→        # check cfn-lint provided schemas
   174→        if rt.name in self._registry_schemas:
   175→            self._schemas[reg.name][rt.name] = self._registry_schemas[rt.name]

   178→        # load the schema

   265→
   266→        Args:
   267→            region (str): the region in which do ge the provider schema for

   269→        Returns:
   270→            None: returns when complete

   273→        suffix = ".cn" if region in ["cn-north-1", "cn-northwest-1"] else ""

   275→        reg = ToPy(region)

   278→            f"{self._root.path_relative}/{self._region_primary.py}/"
   279→        )
   280→
   281→        multiprocessing_logger = multiprocessing.log_to_stderr()
   282→
   283→        multiprocessing_logger.debug("Downloading template %s into %s", url, directory)
   284→
   285→        # Check to see if we already have the latest version, and if so stop
   286→        if not (url_has_newer_version(url) or force):
   287→            return
   288→
   289→        if not os.path.exists(directory):
   290→            os.mkdir(directory)
   291→
   292→        try:
   293→            filehandle = get_url_retrieve(url, caching=True)
   294→            # clean folder
   295→            shutil.rmtree(directory)
   296→            with zipfile.ZipFile(filehandle, "r") as zip_ref:
   297→                zip_ref.extractall(directory)
   298→
   299→            filenames = [

   304→            # There is no schema for CDK but its an allowable type

   306→            with open(f"{directory}module.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:

   314→                    indent=1,
   315→                    separators=(",", ": "),
   316→                    sort_keys=True,
   317→                )
   318→                fh.write("\n")
   319→            for filename in filenames:

   323→
   324→            self._patch_region_schemas(region)

   428→    def _patch_provider_schema(
   429→        self, content: Dict, source_filename: str, region: str

   431→        """Provides the logic to patch a CloudFormation provider schema file.
   432→
   433→        Args:
   434→            content: A Dict representing the data that needs to be patched
   435→            source_filename: The source filename for the JSON patches
   436→            region: The region to apply the patch against
   437→        Returns:
   438→            Dict: returns the patched content
   439→        """
   440→        for patch_type in ["providers", "extensions"]:
   441→            source_dir = source_filename.replace("-", "_").replace(".json", "")
   442→            append_dir = os.path.join(
   443→                self._patches.path_relative, patch_type, region, source_dir
   444→            )
   445→            for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(append_dir):
   446→                filenames.sort()
   447→                for filename in fnmatch.filter(filenames, "*.json"):
   448→                    file_path = os.path.basename(filename)
   449→                    module = dirpath.replace(f"{append_dir}", f"{region}").replace(
   450→                        os.path.sep, "."
   451→                    )
   452→                    try:
   453→                        jsonpatch.JsonPatch(
   454→                            load_resource(
   455→                                f"{self._patches.module}.{patch_type}.{module}.{source_dir}",
   456→                                file_path,
   457→                            )
   458→                        ).apply(content, in_place=True)
   459→                    except jsonpatch.JsonPatchConflict as e:
   460→                        LOGGER.info(
   461→                            "Patch already applied %s: %s",
